title: A generator ships its own self-test, the self-test fails, and no runner ever looks at it
detail: python3 tools/ojz_entity_gen.py test exits 1 on an AssertionError. Invisible because build.sh sweeps test_*.py FILES and these are test_* FUNCTIONS inside a generator module. Confirmed by the controller.

title: A correction sits far below the wrong claim a reader lands on first
detail: Line 11926 heads the section 'NOTHING in them is fixed'; line 12063 says the packet is fully worked. 137 lines apart. Located by content after the seat's own line numbers drifted, which is the same coordinate-rot pattern.

title: The engine's two most-called object entry points document a register as preserved that they overwrite immediately
detail: RunObjects and RunObjects_Frozen write d7 on their first instruction. The machine-checked attribute is correct; the prose is not. Parenthetical is the callee contract sitting on the caller's line.

title: A cache routine's header omits a register its body uses as a live pointer
A comment written to stop a dangerous edit cites a contract that does not exist
detail: TouchResponse over-declares a4 while its body saves and restores it. Over-declaration is unchecked (controller-measured), so nothing stops a reader deleting the movem pair as dead weight, and the comment that exists to stop them names the wrong contract.

title: A spawn routine's contract permits clobbering registers only its prose promises to preserve
detail: Body restores a0/a1/a3 on every path; the attribute licenses clobbering them. Over-declaration is the unchecked direction.

title: An init routine's one-line header is contradicted by its own body comment eight lines below
Five citations point into a file deleted weeks ago, all stale by the same amount
detail: All five match the file as it stood at 560a47be, a uniform +31 offset from its state at deletion. Every substantive claim is TRUE; only the coordinates are wrong. A sibling file cites the same dead file exactly, because it says where to recover it.

title: Every struct field-offset comment in the engine was recomputed and none has drifted
detail: 62 structs, 29 fully sized, 89 offset comments across 9 fully-resolved structs. Red-first control: a mutated offset comment flagged exactly one row.

title: Block geometry can be changed, the one guard that fires can be satisfied exactly as it instructs, and the build goes green with a dozen places still using the old size
detail: Controller measured end to end: BLOCK_TILE_SIZE 16->32 goes red at coll_src_row_base only; doing what that message says ('update the shift') builds green with 17 mask sites still aligning on 16.

title: Plane-wrap masks are spelled two ways in the same files, with nothing holding them in step
A flip-mask comment's arithmetic is wrong in exactly the direction a reader would follow
detail: Comment says $06 = RF_XFLIP|RF_YFLIP, but those are bit NUMBERS so the OR is 3, not 6. Converting the magic number to the named form by following the comment produces the wrong mask.

title: Three explicit branch sizes in a VBlank routine have no argument, where the same file argues all its others
The convention requiring a four-point argument for hardware multiply is unmet at every hand-written site
detail: 9 sites found by two independent instruments. Two are complete; the jump routine's pair meets none of the three applicable points, and its stated reason is one the convention's own 'what does not count' list disposes of.

title: The player-block offset duplication is fully guarded, every constant bound to its struct
detail: 21 consts across 8 files, each with a matching offsetof ensure. Best mechanism found in the sweep.

title: The cache row-stride multiply is open-coded in six places and only two carry a guard
detail: Controller measured: TILE_CACHE_COLS 80->84 goes red at exactly the two guarded sites; fixing both as their messages instruct builds green with four still striding 80. The helper's own doc claims drift is 'unrepresentable'.

title: A parent-chain safety assert exists in two of the four routines that manipulate the chain
detail: The two without it are scaffolding awaiting a consumer, which is what makes it worth fixing now: the first consumer gets the unguarded copy.

title: A proof described as an independent oracle transcribes the code it is checking for most of its fields
detail: The packing derivation is character-identical on both sides for five of nine band fields, so the comparison cannot fail on a wrong packing rule. The file states the correct standard and meets it for one field.

title: Three comptime solvers are duplicated verbatim across two modules with nothing keeping them in step
The file that declares the section descriptor states its size as nearly double what it is
detail: sizeof(Sec) is 34; the header says 66. Controller checked the three out-of-assembler readers: all carry 34, so no wrong stride executes. The stale 66 survives in a second prose site whose own code says 34.

title: A debug surface meant to be read from outside the assembler is described with a layout nothing emits
detail: Reservation describes five slots at one size; the code emits three at another. A consumer decoding by the description reads the wrong offsets. The guard bounds against a hand-copied literal, not the reservation.

title: A stated byte budget for the next ability author is off by one field
The sound driver's timing floor is mirrored as a literal in two modules with no pin on either side
detail: Twelve build-fatal cycle guards consume it. A copy that drifted LOW would not fail; it would make those twelve guards silently accept insufficient hardware spacing.

title: The collected and killed bitmasks have no guard binding their width to the entry count, while an identical twin one block away does
detail: Lowering the offset makes a collected ring silently mark an object dead for the whole act, and the debug assert on the same lines cannot see it because it bounds the index against the number that got out of step.

title: Comments across the engine cite assembler files that no longer exist
detail: engine/constants.asm named 14 times, ram.asm 13, main.asm 11, and roughly 30 more. They read as 'keep this in sync with the other copy'. There is no other copy.

title: Sprite registration reloads a pointer it already holds and shifts one bit further than needed
A parallax loop's stated reason for not being optimised does not hold, but the loop never runs on shipped content
detail: The claimed blocker (no free address register) is refutable. Frequency is zero on the shipped act, so cycles-times-frequency is zero today. One section binding away from being 7.7% of a frame. Recommendation: fix the comment, not the code.

title: Two object pools that are almost entirely empty are swept three times every frame
detail: About 2.2% of a frame. A third pool already keeps a live list and skips empties for free. Structurally invisible to a hot-path walk, which reads the sweep as one call.

title: One of three sibling loops does its setup before the emptiness test rather than after
A collision lookup re-derives per query a value its producers write twice a frame
The obvious saving on the graphics-load routine's register save would corrupt VDP commands
detail: Narrowing the movem to word width sign-extends a destination with bit 15 set into a wrong VDP command word, because the consumer opens with a LONG shift. Recorded as a prohibition so the next reader who spots the same cycles meets it first.

title: Two graphics windows are guarded against a neighbour that is not the one actually next to them
detail: Controller TAG: tightening both to the real neighbour REFUSED with 'unknown name' because the correct symbols are not in those modules' import closure. Adding the imports and keeping the tight bounds builds green, so both are latent. The import closure made the wrong symbol the convenient one.

title: A sprite's tile count can be raised, the build goes green, and it overwrites a different object's graphics
detail: The self-consistent triangle of blob length, byte length and tile count has nothing tying it to the allocated window. The corruption shows up in an unrelated object, only when that object is used.

title: Animation and graphics frame counts are bound together for exactly one asset in the game
detail: The frame reader accepts any byte up to 246 with no upper bound and then reads an offset word from past the offset table. Sonic, Tails, Knuckles, dust, particle, spring and the appendage have no binding.

title: The mechanism that makes every build-time guard real is a manual ritual the build never performs
detail: The prescribed check is a grep of the compiler's warning stream. build.sh contains zero occurrences of it. Compounds the others: the natural repair for them can be placed somewhere its guards never evaluate.

title: The transfer queue's memory layout is assumed contiguous by a routine, guarded by nothing, and the note that says otherwise names a deleted file
detail: Inserting any field between two sub-queues shifts pre-laid register markers so the drain writes transfer parameters into the wrong VDP registers. The note says 'the byte gates are the guard'; that file does not exist and no tool references the symbols.

title: The only net catching a stale sprite cache is debug-only and sits behind a filter the failure itself trips
An interrupt landing in the music-start wait locks the machine up, and the watchdog counts the wrong loop
detail: The bus hold is a latch, not a counter, so the interrupt's own bracket cancels the outer request and nothing below the poll re-issues it. Not reachable in either shipped build; lives in the only profile that can play music.

title: A hardware rule already ruled on was applied to two of the three paths that need it
detail: The third is the one that runs every music tick, and the timer poll sits upstream of the check so the tick structurally cannot see the flag. Symptom is the music going wrong for about a second, periodically.

title: Reading the controllers stops the sound chip for over two drum samples every frame, and a nearby comment says it never happens
detail: Two file headers eight lines apart disagree. The pause is defensible; the audio cost was never written down and one of the two sentences is wrong for the next reader either way.

title: An edit to the sound driver's register contracts builds green here and is caught only in another repo, under an environment variable
detail: Controller verified both halves with a control: removing a register from a Z80 proc's clobber set builds GREEN in aeon with an identical warning summary, while sigil's gate fails immediately and its control on the clean tree passes. Our docs mention that gate once, in a path table, never as a ritual.

title: Two deletions are justified by claiming a routine touches no video hardware, and that routine writes the control port in a loop
detail: Controller verified all three halves, including that the loop's own comment says THIS WRITES THE VDP DIRECTLY in capitals, and that it landed three days after the deletion its absence justified. The conclusion survives only via a guard in another module that advertises itself as revocable.

title: An unmasked command-then-data sequence exists with no callers yet
The raster timing calibration depends on what the main loop is doing, and the instrument that validates it holds that fixed
detail: Its 'zero spread' evidence is what a pinned mainline phase looks like, not what a jitter-free path looks like. The dense tier has no spin at all and fires many times a frame. The falsifier is written so a refutation is the more useful result.

title: Cancelling a background transition can leave the parallax briefly inert, freezing the whole field for a frame
detail: Controller verified both orders: the writer clears the target before the frame count, and the reader tests the frame count then loads the target, so one instruction boundary reads live-but-empty. Every cancelled transition opens it. Fix is swapping two stores.

title: A latch that exists to give three readers one consistent camera is written one field at a time with no protection
detail: Its worst case, a whole-frame raster dropout, is blocked only by shipped content happening to have non-overlapping bands. Nothing enforces that; overlapping bands are authorable today. The same latch's other call site IS protected, deliberately.

title: A busy flag is raised after the work it guards is already queued, costing a lost decode frame
A tearing consumer is missing from the very list that argues why tearing is safe on that path
detail: The conclusion survives. An enumeration that omits a member is the shape that goes wrong later.

title: An install routine publishes its two pointers in the order its own banner argues against
detail: Latent: the sole caller already cleared the cell thousands of cycles earlier. The defence is the caller's, not this routine's, so a second caller re-opens it silently.

title: Six shared-state hazards were traced and proven safe, each with what would have broken it
detail: Includes that a register-packing choice is doing load-bearing atomicity work its own comments describe only as role-swap logic, and that the interrupt handler's mask flavour was chosen to close a one-instruction window.

title: The expensive spawn check runs before the cheap one, on every entity, against what the architecture document already describes
detail: Controller verified: the nine-slot scan sits nine lines before the single bit test, both branching to the same label. The architecture doc says already-loaded entities should be one bit test and skip. Candidate cause for an open worry that has never had one named.

title: A per-entry answer is recomputed for every candidate inside the walk
The despawner rebuilds an address its sibling walks with a pointer, and the sibling states the cure
A value is computed, discarded, and immediately recomputed by a loop whose cost grows with the world size
detail: Low today at the shipped grid, flagged because the mega-act goal is exactly what raises the dimension this loop is linear in.

title: The streaming and residency systems were assessed at the algorithm level and are the right shapes
detail: The staged-block lookup is already hashed, the prefetch deletes its own walk when the act fits, sprites dispatch from insertion-built bands rather than a sort, and palette composition gates every layer behind a staleness bit argued as the same answer rather than an approximation.

title: Two drum samples are stored twice, byte for byte, inside a bank that is almost full
detail: Controller verified both pairs identical with cmp. The free tail today fits one of the six S3K drums; after dedupe it fits all six. The two descriptor ids are indistinguishable at runtime.

title: A stated memory span is nearly half again as large as the comment claims
detail: The banner names a capability set that stopped being the shipped one twice, and was itself edited after both changes. The guard is correct; the prose misprices any future trade against it.

title: The debug build's extra memory is understated by a third of the headroom that remains
detail: Two whole instrument blocks are not counted at all. Each carries a written rationale, so the cost is deliberate; the accounting is what went stale.

title: A palette staging buffer reserves space for a line the build makes impossible
detail: Proven from both ends: unwritable because the authoring layer refuses that line, unreachable because the consumer indexes in at a compile-time offset. Too small to justify a repin alone.

title: Two player history buffers are written every frame and read by nothing
detail: Enumerated by reference across the whole tree. The named future consumer is live work, so this is recorded rather than proposed for deletion.

title: Sonic is the only character whose graphics window has no overrun guard, while both others have one
detail: Peak is 29 of 32 tiles. A re-exported sheet would DMA past the window into the next object's tiles with nothing noticing. Zero-byte fix, and it should precede any attempt to reclaim the spare tiles.

title: A quarter of our test suite maintains a style checker whose subject is eight lines containing no code
detail: Controller verified: it lints a directives-only file and exits clean, under 412 test functions, and the one test asserting the subject has not collapsed skips on a file that was deleted. A red-first control proves the tool itself works.

title: Our only proof that a build-time check can fail covers a small fraction of them, concentrated where coverage already was
detail: Not a demonstrated vacuity: one pair of the uncovered family is on record as proven red. The finding is the absence of a standing net, which is a weaker and more honest claim.

title: Several sets of tests and the harnesses that prove our checks can fail are unreachable by any runner
detail: Includes the compression format's only structural test. Two of the unreachable harnesses are described in the build script's own comments as proving their gate red.

title: Two test classes always skip on a clean tree because they run before the thing they inspect is built
detail: A skip reads as a pass in every aggregate, and the build reads only the exit status. Seven other gates were already moved below the build for exactly this reason.

title: The build script's own description of its test lane is stale by several times, and its self-check does not measure what it claims
An exhaustive scan for the one-keystroke vacuity pattern found none in the engine's entire guard corpus
detail: All conditions parsed, statically-true disjuncts evaluated against every literal constant; the seven that resolve true are all narrow rather than vacuous, and each was traced to its real checker.

title: Register contracts are machine-checked in one direction only, and not at all for the sound processor
detail: Three of the four cells are unguarded from inside this repo. The conventions document states they are compiler-verified. Measured with three builds plus a cross-repo gate and its control.

title: The nightly safety net has not completed a run in nine nights and cannot clear itself
detail: A listing-reading check runs before the build that produces the listing, so it fails on stale data, aborts the build, and the data stays stale. Nine different master revisions failed identically because none was ever built. Reproduced live in the main tree after a merge.

title: This repository has no continuous integration at all
detail: No workflows on the remote and zero workflow runs ever, with an authenticated client. Not a defect by itself; it means the nightly timer was the only backstop, and it was down.

title: A hundred animation guards suspected of never running were measured live
detail: Seat V nominated them and declined to guess, noting its own instrument over-predicts. They are not in the unreachable list. The listing then surfaced eighty-three others, of which seventy-one were proven live by a mutation red on its own row, and the rest belong to the other game. Zero genuinely dead.

title: Whether the raster timing calibration drifts under load needs the emulator to settle
detail: Seat C3a's experiment and falsifier are written and adopted verbatim, including its instruction that a refutation is the more useful result and that a confirming run must not ride on the mechanism story.
